Subject: Staged evaluation to commitment — marketplace purchase plan

Hi Lisa —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our call, I put together a concise staged evaluation -> commitment plan that aligns the marketplace private-offer route (AWS Private Offers) with your procurement and finance gates. The attached MAP spreadsheet breaks the work into three sprints: Eval, Acceptance, and Billing/signature.

Key highlights (high level):
- Eval sprint (2 weeks): focused tests on a representative workload, perf/latency & integration smoke tests, and a short quality sign-off by your ML infra team.
- Acceptance sprint (1 week): finalize production config, cutover plan, and compliance checks (data retention & audit log access).
- Billing & purchase (2–3 weeks): AWS private-offer flow requires a private-offer acceptance + Redwood invoice routing. We include optional marketplace billing (charge via AWS) or direct invoiced purchase — both documented in the sheet.

Immediate asks for Acme:
1) Confirm a technical lead for the Eval sprint (name + email).
2) Confirm whether your finance team prefers Marketplace billing (AWS charges) or vendor-invoice (Redwood invoices Acme).
3) Any mandatory legal terms we should address up front (NDA already signed).

I've attached: MAP_AcmeApps_v1.xlsx (action plan and dates), Redwood_PrivateOffer_Terms_v1.pdf (sample payment & SOW terms), and a small invoice-path-diagram.png that maps the two billing options.

Proposed timeline (we can shift to fit your procurement windows):
- Nov 9: Kickoff (today)
- Nov 10–23: Eval sprint (tests + demos)
- Nov 24–30: Acceptance & final config
- Dec 1–14: Billing/PO & sign-off -> production enablement

If these windows look reasonable, we'll run the MAP as the mutual checklist and treat the spreadsheet as the single source of truth. I can update it live as approvals come in.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: MAP_AcmeApps_v1.xlsx; Redwood_PrivateOffer_Terms_v1.pdf; invoice-path-diagram.png

Thanks, Mateo — this is helpful.

Quick answers:
- Technical lead: Ben Kwan (ben.kwan@acmeapps.com), I'll add him to the MAP sheet shortly.
- Finance preference: we prefer Marketplace billing where possible (have had an easier time reconciling charges through our cloud invoices). However, our finance team may accept a vendor invoice for larger commitments.
- Legal: our procurement team will push for a standard data processing addendum and invoice net-30. I'll loop in legal if we need redlines.

Two asks from our side: can you indicate which testing artifacts you need (sample logs, perf counters, or a synthetic load script)? Also, can you confirm support coverage during the Eval sprint (on-call window)?

I'll review the MAP with procurement and reply with a firm go/no-go by EOD Thursday (Nov 12).

—Lisa

Hi Lisa / Ben —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. To answer both of your asks:

Testing artifacts we need (minimal set):
- Synthetic load script (we can provide a JMeter script or a small Python harness)
- Example input set (5–10 representative prompts) and expected success criteria (latency P95 <= 450ms for 1–2k token requests)
- Sample log capture instructions (we'll provide a logging snippet you can drop into your integration)

Support coverage during the Eval sprint:
- Redwood will provide a named SE (me) plus an on-call engineer (overnight UTC-8 coverage Mon–Fri 9a–5p PST, and limited weekend support for scheduled tests). If you need 24/7 coverage for stress tests, we can provision an extended support add-on (we should budget for that).

I've also updated the MAP spreadsheet (v1) with a detailed checklist and assigned tentative owners. Key dates now reflect Ben as the technical lead for your side.

About billing: because you prefer marketplace billing, note two operational details for AWS Private Offer flows:
1) AWS will reflect charges on your EC2/AWS bill; the private-offer acceptance is done in the AWS Console and requires a contact email and a redemption action.
2) Redwood still issues a contract and can optionally invoice (Redwood invoices are standard net-30). If you choose marketplace billing, finance still often requests a Redwood pro-forma invoice for internal approval — happy to provide that.

Next steps:
- Ben: can you confirm availability for a 60-minute kickoff on Nov 12?
- Procurement: confirm Marketplace billing OK by Nov 12 EOD so we can lock the timeline.

Thanks — I'll stand up a calendar invite once Ben confirms.

Cheers,
Mateo

2) Finance needs the pro-forma invoice to route approvals; please include a notional commitment amount for approval (we're estimating a 12-month consumption of ~$180k).

If Redwood provides the pro-forma and we get the redline back, procurement can commit to the AWS private-offer acceptance by the week of Nov 30.

Also, please share the DocuSign link once the final contract is packaged so we can expedite signature.
